data.long_meaning: Thokchom is a Hindu name derived from the Manipuri language. It translates to 'Lord of the Mountain'. This name is inspired by the mythological figure of the same name, who is believed to be the protector of the mountains and a symbol of power, strength, and wisdom. The name Thokchom carries the meaning “Lord of the Mountain” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Hindi, Manipuri. Parents who choose Thokchom usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the mountain and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Thokchom represents the divine energy that resides in the mountains. It is a reminder of the power and strength that lies within us, and the wisdom that can be gained by connecting with nature.
data.etymology: Thokchom belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Mountain.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Thokchom total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: Thokchom was a king of the Kangleipak Kingdom in Manipur, India. He ruled between 1470 and 1500 AD. Thokchom is considered a legendary figure for his wisdom and bravery in the face of foreign invaders. He is best known for his alliance with Ahom king Sukapha, which marked the beginning of the Ahom-Kangleipak relations.
